cues.en: Writing,
cues.zh: 书写，

cues.en: reading,
cues.zh: 阅读，

cues.en: typing,
cues.zh: 打字，

cues.en: texting.
cues.zh: 发短信。

cues.en: Written language is just one of those things that's always been around.
cues.zh: 书面语只是那些一直存在的事物之一。

cues.en: It's a natural way for you to use words. It's a given, but there's something you've forgotten.
cues.zh: 这是你用词的一种自然方式。它理所当然，但有些事你已经忘了。

cues.en: It's understandable. After all, it's been a very long time.
cues.zh: 可以理解。毕竟已经过去很久了。

cues.en: A long time since no one on the planet knew how to write.
cues.zh: 很久了，久到地球上没人会书写。

cues.en: Our story starts with a legend, the tale of Thoth and Thamus.
cues.zh: 我们的故事始于一个传说：Thoth 和 Thamus 的故事。

cues.en: No. That's not a lisp you're hearing. Thoth and Thamus. Thoth and Thamus.
cues.zh: 不。你听到的不是口齿不清。Thoth 和 Thamus。Thoth 和 Thamus。

cues.en: After the Egyptian god, Thoth, invents writing, he runs to king Thamus to share this discovery.
cues.zh: 埃及神托特发明文字后，跑去向国王塔穆斯分享这一发现。

cues.en: But to his chagrin,
cues.zh: 但令他懊恼的是，

cues.en: the king isn't impressed
cues.zh: 国王一点也不为所动，

cues.en: at all.
cues.zh: 完全没被打动。

cues.en: Looking down his nose, he starts pontificating
cues.zh: 他居高临下地开始说教

cues.en: on the destructive power of this newfangled technology.
cues.zh: 大谈这项新奇技术的破坏性力量。

cues.en: Oh, clever Thoth.
cues.zh: 哦，聪明的托特。

cues.en: This invention will produce forgetfulness in the minds of learners with the neglect of their memory because their trust in writing comes from strange external marks and not their own internal recall.
cues.zh: 这项发明会让学习者疏于记忆，从而产生遗忘，因为他们依赖的是外来的奇怪符号，而非自己内在的回忆。

cues.en: The drug you've discovered isn't a memory enhancer,
cues.zh: 你发现的这种药物不是记忆增强剂，

cues.en: but a mentioning enhancer,
cues.zh: 而是提及增强剂，

cues.en: and you're offering students pretend wisdom,
cues.zh: 你提供给学生的是伪智慧，

cues.en: not truth.
cues.zh: 不是真理。

cues.en: This sounds strange. It's easy for you and your world full of writing to dismiss Thamus,
cues.zh: 这听起来很奇怪。对你和你那个充满文字的世界来说，很容易对 Thamus 不屑一顾，

cues.en: but hear him out. He brings you back to the early days of writing when it was the hot new thing.
cues.zh: 但听他把话说完。他把你带回文字的早期，那时它还是热门新事物。

cues.en: And like many other inventions, not everyone was on board.
cues.zh: 和许多其他发明一样，并非所有人都支持。

cues.en: Okay. So let's say, for the sake of argument, you don't want writing.
cues.zh: 好吧。那么，为了论证起见，假设你不想要文字。

cues.en: What are the alternative technologies?
cues.zh: 替代技术有哪些？

cues.en: You could bust out your abacuses.
cues.zh: 你可以把算盘拿出来。

cues.en: They'll help with counting and doing complex calculations.
cues.zh: 它们能帮你计数和做复杂计算。

cues.en: Maybe you prefer icons,
cues.zh: 也许你更喜欢圣像，

cues.en: ritualized images that help you relate to culturally significant figures, events, and attitudes.
cues.zh: 那些仪式化的图像，能帮你关联到文化上重要的人物、事件和观念。

cues.en: The Khifu is an amazing ink and information storage system using cords, colors, and knots.
cues.zh: Khifu 是一套了不起的墨水与信息存储系统，利用绳索、颜色和绳结。

cues.en: Oh, and don't overlook rote memorization.
cues.zh: 哦，也别忽视死记硬背。

cues.en: A basic option, sure. But it's really useful in preliterate societies where sentences can be memorized and recited by the thousands.
cues.zh: 没错，这是基础选项。但在没有文字的社会里非常有用，那里的人们能记住并背诵成千上万的句子。

cues.en: Your brain is bigger than you think.
cues.zh: 你的大脑比你想象的要大。

cues.en: Perhaps you prefer petroglyphs,
cues.zh: 也许你更喜欢岩画，

cues.en: rock carvings with major cultural ties that may refer to nearby places or animals.
cues.zh: 这些岩刻与重要文化紧密相关，可能指代附近的地点或动物。

cues.en: Oh, watch out writing. We're getting uncomfortably close.
cues.zh: 哦，当心书写。我们正靠得近得让人不舒服。

cues.en: All of these inventions helped humans keep track of their thoughts. So what makes writing different?
cues.zh: 所有这些发明都帮助人类记录自己的想法。那么书写有什么不同？

cues.en: What's Thamus afraid of? Let's talk some ness,
cues.zh: 塔穆斯害怕什么？咱们聊聊“性”——嵌入性。

cues.en: embeddedness.
cues.zh: 嵌入性。

cues.en: These things are all embedded in minds, tasks, rituals, events, cultures.
cues.zh: 这些东西都嵌入在头脑、任务、仪式、事件、文化之中。

cues.en: Rip them from those contexts and you rip out their expressive heart.
cues.zh: 把它们从那些语境中剥离出来，就等于挖掉了它们表达力的核心。

cues.en: Thoth's drug doesn't come with so many strings attached.
cues.zh: Thoth 的药可没那么多附加条件。

cues.en: It will de embed you, letting you record any specific thought and letting future generations read it in any context.
cues.zh: 它会把你从语境中抽离出来，让你记录下任何具体的想法，并让后代能在任何语境中读到它。

cues.en: So human,
cues.zh: 所以，人类，

cues.en: was Thamus right? Is writing an unnatural intrusion?
cues.zh: Thamus 说得对吗？文字是一种不自然的侵入吗？

cues.en: Or do you want to swallow Thoth's pill and see for yourself what we actually unleashed when we invented writing?
cues.zh: 还是你想吞下 Thoth 的药丸，亲眼看看我们发明文字时究竟释放出了什么？

cues.en: La France,
cues.zh: 法国，

cues.en: seventeen thousand years ago.
cues.zh: 一万七千年前。

cues.en: It's cold out and getting colder,
cues.zh: 外面很冷，而且越来越冷，

cues.en: possibly dangerous too.
cues.zh: 可能还很危险。

cues.en: This may be France and this may be the history of writing, but there's nothing for you here.
cues.zh: 这里可能是法国，也可能是书写的历史，但这里没有你要找的东西。

cues.en: Until you take shelter in a nearby cave and see how creative some of your ancestors really were.
cues.zh: 直到你在附近的洞穴里避难，看到你的祖先有多富有创造力。

cues.en: Drawing on their enlarging brains and a long prehistory of building ever more complex tools,
cues.zh: 凭借不断增大的大脑和建造越来越复杂工具的漫长史前经验，

cues.en: these early artists took to etching and painting beautiful visual representations of the animals around them. These aren't words,
cues.zh: 这些早期艺术家开始蚀刻和绘制周围动物的美丽视觉形象。这些不是文字，

cues.en: they're not stories,
cues.zh: 它们不是故事，

cues.en: they're pictures.
cues.zh: 它们是图画。

cues.en: Early pictures like these start to become very routine, not necessarily depicting the world, but marking and standing for things.
cues.zh: 像这样的早期图画开始变得司空见惯，不一定是在描绘世界，而是在标记并指代事物。

cues.en: A place to hunt,
cues.zh: 一个狩猎的地方，

cues.en: a place to eat. These are pictographs.
cues.zh: 一个进食的地方。这些是象形图。

cues.en: The story gets sketchy here, but it's important to notice that pictographic symbols like these petroglyphs,
cues.zh: 故事到这里变得模糊了，但重要的是要注意，像这些岩画这样的象形符号，

cues.en: rock carvings, weren't words. They weren't language,
cues.zh: 石刻，并不是词语。它们不是语言，

cues.en: but they became more than personal and communal artistic expressions.
cues.zh: 但它们超越了个人和群体的艺术表达。

cues.en: They became regular and repeatable,
cues.zh: 它们变得规整、可重复，

cues.en: possibly mapping to specific things. And for that, these pictographs earned themselves the fancy label of proto writing.
cues.zh: 可能对应到具体事物。正因如此，这些图画文字得了个高级名号：原始文字。

cues.en: Many pictographs have an intuitive giveaway quality.
cues.zh: 许多图画文字有一种直观易懂的特质。

cues.en: They look like drawings of the things they represent.
cues.zh: 它们看起来就像所代表事物的图画。

cues.en: Draw me a human. Easy. Draw me a horse. Sure.
cues.zh: 给我画个人。简单。画匹马。没问题。

cues.en: A river? There it is. But how do you clearly and simply draw less tangible ideas, like playing around or taking it easy or don't even think about it? Uh-oh.
cues.zh: 河流？就在那儿。但像“随便玩玩”“放轻松”或者“想都别想”这类不太有形的想法，怎么清楚又简单地画出来呢？哎呀。

cues.en: Watch out for this. Major moments in the history of writing.
cues.zh: 注意这一点。这是书写史上的重大时刻。

cues.en: Meet metonymy.
cues.zh: 认识一下转喻。

cues.en: This principled fellow lets you represent a general nebulous idea with a related pictogram or part of a pictogram or a pictogram combo that's pretty specific and obvious.
cues.zh: 这位讲原则的家伙，能让你用一个相关的象形图、或象形图的一部分、或一个相当具体直观的象形图组合，来表达一个笼统模糊的概念。

cues.en: Ancient stick human is a regular old pictogram.
cues.zh: 古代的棍状小人就是普通的象形图。

cues.en: If you cut off stick's legs, you can get across the general idea of what?
cues.zh: 如果把小人的腿去掉，你能传达出什么笼统概念？

cues.en: Walking or moving? What about a man leaning against a tree? What's the idea here?
cues.zh: 走路或移动？那一个人靠在树边呢？这里表达的是什么概念？

cues.en: Taking it easy.
cues.zh: 放轻松。

cues.en: Resting.
cues.zh: 休息。

cues.en: These are ideographs,
cues.zh: 这些是表意文字，

cues.en: symbols for ideas and concepts.
cues.zh: 表示想法和概念的符号。

cues.en: In some sense, all of these drawings express ideas, the concept of a horse, the concept of a human. So they're all ideographic.
cues.zh: 某种意义上，这些图画都在表达想法：马的概念、人的概念。所以它们都是表意的。

cues.en: But with a little imagination and a lot of time, extended ideographs let you cut and combine basic pictographs to be far more expressive and abstract.
cues.zh: 但只要有点想象力，再加上大量时间，扩展的表意文字就能让你切割、组合基本象形文字，从而更有表现力、也更抽象。

cues.en: Just when you're ready to grab that chisel and get your pictographic and ideographic carving on, someone more inventive than you comes along.
cues.zh: 就在你准备拿起凿子，开始刻你的象形文字和表意文字时，总会冒出个比你更有创意的人。

cues.en: Your pictures and ideas aren't enough for her.
cues.zh: 你的图画和想法对她来说还不够。

cues.en: Gone are the days of Lascaux.
cues.zh: 拉斯科的时代已经过去了。

cues.en: The world outside this cave is changing, she says. Crops, cities, rulers, markets, and she needs a way to keep track of it all. She likes your icons. She can use them for goats and pots, fields, and even long walks through the desert.
cues.zh: 她说，这个洞穴外的世界正在改变：庄稼、城市、统治者、市场，她需要一种方法来记录这一切。她喜欢你的图标。她可以用它们表示山羊和陶罐、田地，甚至穿越沙漠的长途跋涉。

cues.en: But she has an incredible practical streak. She takes those goats and those pots and starts to tally the items she's recording.
cues.zh: 但她非常务实。她拿起那些山羊和陶罐，开始统计她正在记录的东西。

cues.en: One goat, she says, then two goats, three goats, four goats.
cues.zh: 她说，一只山羊，然后是两只山羊、三只山羊、四只山羊。

cues.en: Notice what she's done. These aren't simple depictions anymore. They're not just ideas.
cues.zh: 注意她做了什么。这些不再是简单的描绘，也不只是想法。

cues.en: She's reading one word for each symbol.
cues.zh: 她为每个符号读出一个词。

cues.en: She's encoding language.
cues.zh: 她在编码语言。

cues.en: Let's slow down here because it's hard to overstate the importance of this major
cues.zh: 我们在这里放慢一点，因为很难夸大这个重要

cues.en: moments in the history of writing.
cues.zh: 时刻在书写史上的意义。

cues.en: These goat counts are word symbols now,
cues.zh: 这些山羊计数现在是词符，

cues.en: logographs.
cues.zh: 是表词符号。

cues.en: Pictographs can be visualized,
cues.zh: 象形符号可以被看见，

cues.en: ideographs can be imagined,
cues.zh: 表意符号可以被想象，

cues.en: but logographs can be directly and consistently read.
cues.zh: 但表词符号可以被直接而一致地读出来。

cues.en: Logographic systems emerge and flourish in the early civilizations of Mesopotamia,
cues.zh: 表意文字系统在美索不达米亚、

cues.en: Egypt, China, and Mexico.
cues.zh: 埃及、中国和墨西哥的早期文明中诞生并兴盛。

cues.en: Characters for people, animals, land, crops, hundreds, even thousands of logographs for everything under the sun and moon, including the sun and the moon. Even after all these millennia,
cues.zh: 有表示人、动物、土地、农作物的字符，还有成百甚至上千个表意文字，涵盖日月之下的一切，包括太阳和月亮。即便过了几千年，

cues.en: if you squint hard enough, you can still pick out the symbols scratched into weathered artifacts bearing the world's early scripts. A Chinese turtle, an Egyptian house, a Sumerian head, a Sumerian head eating bread, a Mayan jaguar.
cues.zh: 只要眯起眼睛仔细看，仍能在风化文物上辨认出刻着的符号，它们承载着世界早期文字。中国的龟、埃及的房子、苏美尔人的头、一个正在吃面包的苏美尔人的头、玛雅的美洲豹。

cues.en: And in each of these places, in all of these languages,
cues.zh: 而在这些地方，在所有这类语言中，

cues.en: these were read as words.
cues.zh: 这些符号都被当作词来读。

cues.en: We know what these logographs mean, and we can put that meaning into words.
cues.zh: 我们知道这些表意符号是什么意思，也能把这种意思用词表达出来。

cues.en: The world is now in a race to fill itself with logographs.
cues.zh: 如今，全世界都在竞相用表意符号填满自己。

cues.en: But which humans started this craze?
cues.zh: 但哪一群人开启了这股风潮？

cues.en: Well, the Mesoamerican
cues.zh: 嗯，中美洲人

cues.en: started writing more than twenty nine hundred years ago. Some Chinese characters are at least 3,200
cues.zh: 在两千九百多年前就开始书写了。有些汉字至少有3,200

cues.en: years old. Writing popped up in Crete four thousand years ago.
cues.zh: 年历史。四千年前，书写在克里特岛出现。

cues.en: But the two clear contenders are Egyptian hieroglyphs and Sumerian cuneiform,
cues.zh: 但两个明确的竞争者是埃及象形文字和苏美尔楔形文字，

cues.en: both a whopping 5,000
cues.zh: 两者都足足有5000年

cues.en: years old,
cues.zh: 历史，

cues.en: minimum.
cues.zh: 至少。

cues.en: It's common to say that the Egyptians stole the idea of writing from Mesopotamia and just came up with their own glyphs.
cues.zh: 人们常说，埃及人从美索不达米亚偷来了书写这个点子，只是自己另造了字形。

cues.en: Common, but not demonstrated.
cues.zh: 这说法很常见，但并未得到证实。

cues.en: For a while, monogenesis made sense. This is the idea that one civilization was king of all the writing. That writing started once in Mesopotamia,
cues.zh: 有一段时间，单一起源论说得通。这种观点认为，某一个文明是全部书写的王者。书写只在美索不达米亚起源过一次，

cues.en: where people pressed a stylus into wet clay to make these wedge,
cues.zh: 在那里，人们把笔按进湿黏土，压出这些楔形、

cues.en: cuneus, shapes,
cues.zh: cuneus，形状，

cues.en: forms, cuneiform.
cues.zh: 形态，也就是楔形文字。

cues.en: So the monogenesis story goes. Everyone else steals cuneiform and reskins it to fit their own needs. It's not a popular story these days, given what we know about Chinese and especially Mesoamerican writing, along with some very early Egyptian finds.
cues.zh: 单一起源说就是这么讲的：其他所有人都偷来楔形文字，换层皮来满足自己的需求。如今这说法不太流行了，毕竟我们对中国文字、尤其是中美洲文字有所了解，还有一些非常早期的埃及考古发现。

cues.en: Whoever's first. In these early days of writing, all the civilizations start manufacturing hoards of logographs.
cues.zh: 谁先谁后都一样。在文字诞生初期，所有文明都开始大量制造表意符号。

cues.en: So many, in fact, that they unwittingly unleash an epic memory burden on budding logographers
cues.zh: 多到他们无意间给初学表意文字的人带来了巨大的记忆负担，

cues.en: from would be ancient scribes to beginning students of Mandarin Chinese.
cues.zh: 从想成为古代书吏的人，到初学普通话的学生。

cues.en: Do they really need this many characters to write? Surely there's an easier way.
cues.zh: 他们真的需要这么多字来写吗？肯定有更省事的办法吧。

cues.en: Say hello to this smart rogue who's about to solve your problem with an innocent mistake.
cues.zh: 来认识一下这个机灵的小捣蛋鬼，他马上要用一个无心之误帮你解决问题。

cues.en: His father has been counting sheep,
cues.zh: 他爸爸一直在数羊，

cues.en: literally,
cues.zh: 真的是在数羊，

cues.en: and he just asked his son to record a measly line in his budget.
cues.zh: 他刚让儿子在预算里记上微不足道的一笔。

cues.en: 10 sheep for uncle.
cues.zh: 给叔叔记十只羊。

cues.en: The son writes the 10 and the logograph for sheep, but uncle?
cues.zh: 儿子写下“10”和表示“羊”的字，可“叔叔”呢？

cues.en: He pauses and scratches his head. Eager to play with his friends, he writes the character for ankle. 10 sheep,
cues.zh: 他停顿一下，挠挠头。急着去和朋友玩，他写下了“踝”字。十只羊，

cues.en: ankle.
cues.zh: 脚踝。

cues.en: He hurries away without a second thought, but don't take his invention lightly.
cues.zh: 他毫不犹豫地匆匆离开，但别小看他的发明。

cues.en: If you've ever played fill in the blank or guessing games where you have to sound out picture words, you've seen and used this principle for yourself.
cues.zh: 如果你玩过填空或猜词游戏，需要把图片对应的词读出来，那你就已经见过并用过这个原理。

cues.en: But it's not just for quirky puzzles with funny solutions.
cues.zh: 但它可不只用于那些答案滑稽的古怪谜题。

cues.en: The name for this is another... Major moments in the history of writing. The
cues.zh: 它的名字是另一个……书写史上的重大时刻。这个

cues.en: name for this is is Rebus.
cues.zh: 这个的名称就是 Rebus。

cues.en: This familiar language game lets you look beyond the meaning of a character and use it simply for its sound.
cues.zh: 这种熟悉的语言游戏让你越过字符的含义，只按它的读音来用。

cues.en: Sun sounds like sun and, by extension, perhaps soon and sewn. Logographs,
cues.zh: Sun 听起来像 sun，推而广之，也许还像 soon 和 sewn。词符，

cues.en: like the symbol for sun, could already be read as words. Now with the rebus principle in your pocket, logographs can also be read as sounds.
cues.zh: 比如太阳的符号，已经可以被读成词了。现在掌握了画谜原则，词符也可以被读成声音。

cues.en: This isn't just useful for getting ancient uncle his ancient sheep. Once Aztec city planners finished building their stunning capital in the middle of a lake, the Venice of the New World, Tenochtitlan,
cues.zh: 这不仅有助于给古代叔叔弄到他的古代绵羊。一旦阿兹特克城市规划者完成在湖中央建造他们令人惊叹的首都——新世界的威尼斯，特诺奇蒂特兰，

cues.en: their scribes needed a way to write its name.
cues.zh: 他们的书吏就需要一种写出它名字的方法。

cues.en: They've been using what amounts to basic picture writing.
cues.zh: 他们用的其实相当于基础的图画文字。

cues.en: Since Tenochtitlan
cues.zh: 既然 Tenochtitlan

cues.en: has a stone, te, and a cactus, Nochli,
cues.zh: 有石头 te，还有仙人掌 Nochli，

cues.en: it's natural to write it with two fairly obvious glyphs.
cues.zh: 自然就用两个相当明显的字形来写它。

cues.en: Then these become not just symbols meaning cactus and stone, but symbols for the noises, Tenochtitlan,
cues.zh: 于是它们不再只是表示仙人掌和石头的符号，而成了表示这些读音的符号——Tenochtitlan，

cues.en: making them just as much rebus fun as those puzzles you solved as a kid. And now you know the name for those. You also know why there's a cactus on top of a stone in Mexico's flag. It's not just for show.
cues.zh: 这让它们像你小时候解的那些谜题一样，充满画谜的乐趣。现在你知道这类谜题叫什么了。你也知道为什么墨西哥国旗上仙人掌长在石头上。这可不只是装饰。

cues.en: How alike does a sound alike pronunciation have to be? Which sounds can we chop off? Pit the Egyptians against the Sumerians one more time. Egyptian hieroglyphs cut off the initial consonant or less often two or three consonants from the original word.
cues.zh: 读音相似到底要多相似？哪些音可以砍掉？再让埃及人和苏美尔人较量一次。埃及圣书体从原词中砍掉开头的辅音，或者较少见地砍掉两三个辅音。

cues.en: Sumerians,
cues.zh: 苏美尔人，

cues.en: on the other hand, with their cuneiform,
cues.zh: 另一方面，用他们的楔形文字，

cues.en: take whole syllables.
cues.zh: 取的是整个音节。

cues.en: These two paths don't just add some local flavor.
cues.zh: 这两条路径可不只是添了点地方色彩。

cues.en: Revising out consonants doesn't just impact ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs.
cues.zh: 删去辅音并不只影响古埃及圣书体。

cues.en: It leaves a legacy for later spin offs, the mentality that these are either read as logographs or they stand for consonants.
cues.zh: 它为后来的衍生文字留下了一份遗产：一种观念——这些符号要么被读作表意文字，要么代表辅音。

cues.en: Cuneiform leaves a different legacy.
cues.zh: 楔形文字留下了另一种遗产。

cues.en: Completely unrelated languages will spend thousands of years borrowing and reborrowing cuneiform to write their own words.
cues.zh: 完全无关的语言会用数千年不断借用、再借用楔形文字来书写自己的词语。

cues.en: But each time, the symbols are read as logographs or as syllables.
cues.zh: 但每一次，这些符号都被读作表意文字或音节。

cues.en: Flexibility is key here. Look at this Egyptian hieroglyph.
cues.zh: 灵活性是关键。看看这个埃及象形文字。

cues.en: It can be read as the logograph for mouth, re, or as the consonant, r.
cues.zh: 它可以被解读为表示“嘴”的意符 re，或者辅音 r。

cues.en: This character could be read as the logograph meaning house,
cues.zh: 这个字符可以被读作意为“房屋”的意符，

cues.en: or it could stand for the consonant, pr, the two consonants in the Egyptian word. Conveniently, in Egyptian, the little slashy below lets you know when it's a pure logograph.
cues.zh: 或者它可以代表辅音 pr，即埃及语单词中的两个辅音。方便的是，在埃及语中，下方的小斜线能让你知道它何时是纯意符。

cues.en: The rebus discovery brings up a tension between meaning and sound.
cues.zh: 画谜的发现揭示了意义与声音之间的张力。

cues.en: Is writing phonetic or semantic?
cues.zh: 书写是表音的还是表意的？

cues.en: Is it about encoding the meaning of words or encoding speech sounds?
cues.zh: 这是在编码词的含义，还是编码语音？

cues.en: The old logographs were fundamentally a meaning writing system.
cues.zh: 古代的表意文字本质上是一种表意书写系统。

cues.en: Sure, this sounds like re in Egyptian, but what's crucial is that this is a logograph for the word meaning mouth.
cues.zh: 当然，这听起来像埃及语里的 re，但关键是，这是一个表示“嘴”这个词的语标。

cues.en: Rebus writing takes a big step towards sound writing.
cues.zh: 画谜文字向表音文字迈出了一大步。

cues.en: This will come to stand for the consonant r regardless
cues.zh: 这将最终代表辅音 r，无论

cues.en: of meaning.
cues.zh: 含义如何。

cues.en: It may come as a surprise, but once discovered,
cues.zh: 这也许令人意外，但一旦被发现，

cues.en: sound writing doesn't oust meaning writing, not at all.
cues.zh: 表音文字并没有取代表意文字，完全没有。

cues.en: Indeed, early writers noticed that phonetic writing brings up a problem, a problem you probably missed because of your comfort with sound writing, a problem that meaning writing can solve. Brace yourself, history, because logographs are about to make a comeback.
cues.zh: 确实，早期书写者注意到，表音文字会带来一个问题；由于你习惯了表音书写，很可能忽略了这个问题；而表意书写可以解决它。历史，做好准备吧，因为表意文字要回归了。

cues.en: Like all of the world's earliest writing systems, Chinese characters start out as symbols that stand for words. A rice paddy,
cues.zh: 和世界上所有最早的文字系统一样，汉字最初也是代表词语的符号。一块稻田，

cues.en: a person,
cues.zh: 一个人，

cues.en: a tree.
cues.zh: 一棵树。

cues.en: These are logographs, and they let you depict specific language pieces to write what you mean. But instead of requiring different characters for every word, the handy rebus principle lets you write other things that sound like the logograph to write what you say.
cues.zh: 这些是表意文字，能让你描绘特定的语言单位，写出你想表达的意思。但它不需要每个词都用不同字符，而是靠方便的“画谜原则”，用发音像该表意文字的其他东西来写下你要说的话。

cues.en: Sure. You could use the rebus sounds like principle to write any sound in your language,
cues.zh: 当然。你可以用画谜的“听起来像”原则，写出你语言里的任何发音，

cues.en: but please consider this symbol and answer the question that follows.
cues.zh: 但请看看这个符号，然后回答接下来的问题。

cues.en: Does it mean sun,
cues.zh: 它是指“太阳”（sun），

cues.en: soon,
cues.zh: “很快”（soon），

cues.en: sun, or sewn?
cues.zh: “太阳”（sun），还是“缝好”（sewn）？

cues.en: Oh my, did Rebus writing get you into a bit of trouble here?
cues.zh: 哎呀，画谜式写法是不是让你有点犯难了？

cues.en: When we see this character, we could read it as a plain old logograph according to its meaning or any of these Rebus ways following its pronunciation.
cues.zh: 看到这个字时，我们可以按含义把它当作普通的表意文字，也可以按发音用这些画谜方式来读。

cues.en: Which one should you choose?
cues.zh: 该选哪一个？

cues.en: Think a bit outside of the jade box here and take the lead of this Han scribe.
cues.zh: 这里要稍微跳出“玉盒”的框框，跟着这位汉代书吏的思路走。

cues.en: His solution is elegant.
cues.zh: 他的解法很优雅。

cues.en: Don't choose one.
cues.zh: 别只选一种。

cues.en: Use both systems together.
cues.zh: 把两套系统一起用。

cues.en: What's that behind his back? Is that a, oh, yeah.
cues.zh: 他背后那是什么？那是……哦，对。

cues.en: Major moments in the history of writing.
cues.zh: 书写史上的重大时刻。

cues.en: So here's the logograph for horse, but it also sounds the same as the word for ant. So the Rebus principle lets us write them both with the same glyph.
cues.zh: 这是“马”的表意字，但它的发音和“蚂蚁”这个词相同。于是画谜原则让我们用同一个字形来写这两个词。

cues.en: Confusing?
cues.zh: 会混淆吗？

cues.en: Not if you add the logograph for insect next to the sound alike character.
cues.zh: 如果在同音字旁边加上“昆虫”的表意字，就不会了。

cues.en: This says it's pronounced like horse, which it is, but that its meaning has something to do with insect.
cues.zh: 这表示它的读音像“马”——确实如此——但意思和昆虫有关。

cues.en: You don't read the extra character, it's a meaning hint, determining how to read the sound character. So it's called a determinative.
cues.zh: 多出来的那个字不用读，它是意义提示，决定表音字怎么读。所以叫义符。

cues.en: One more Mandarin example. This logograph means moon, which happens to be pronounced Using
cues.zh: 再举一个普通话例子。这个汉字表示月亮，恰好读作 Using

cues.en: rebus writing, also
cues.zh: 借音书写，也

cues.en: means amputate your feet. Incidentally,
cues.zh: 意思是截去双脚。顺便一提，

cues.en: the word key is pronounced the same way. Same problem.
cues.zh: key 这个词发音相同。同样的问题。

cues.en: But nothing a couple determinatives can't fix.
cues.zh: 但几个义符就能搞定。

cues.en: Add the determinative for metal to this character.
cues.zh: 给这个字加上表示金属的义符。

cues.en: Add knife to that one. And let's leave the moon be because that's already what it means.
cues.zh: 给那个字加上“刀”。月亮就先别动，因为它本来就是那个意思。

cues.en: Here again, the sounds like reading of a character gives you its phonetic component.
cues.zh: 这里也一样，字的相近读音给出了它的声旁。

cues.en: This extra logograph clues you into its meaning, its semantic component.
cues.zh: 这个多出来的字形提示它的含义，也就是它的形旁。

cues.en: Together, they form a unit, a whole character with a clear meaning and a clear pronunciation.
cues.zh: 合在一起，它们构成一个整体，一个意思清楚、读音清楚的完整汉字。

cues.en: Determinatives
cues.zh: 义符

cues.en: are very common in Chinese characters, natively called Han characters.
cues.zh: 在汉字中非常常见，汉字的本族名称就是 Han characters。

cues.en: In fact, since they hint at the character's root meaning, it's radix,
cues.zh: 事实上，既然它们暗示了字符的根本含义，那就是 radix，

cues.en: Han determinatives get called radicals.
cues.zh: 汉字的表意构件被称为部首。

cues.en: Bringing back the character's son, it can be pronounced many ways. True. But add a determinative,
cues.zh: 回到这个字里的“子”，它可以有很多种读音。没错。但加上一个意符，

cues.en: a silent helper character, and you can quickly narrow down its meaning. These extra determinatives avoid ambiguous readings.
cues.zh: 一个不发音的辅助字，就能快速缩小它的含义范围。这些额外的意符能避免歧义读法。

cues.en: Which one is the sun in the sky? Which is a father's son? Which one means soon? Too easy.
cues.zh: 哪个是天上的太阳？哪个是父亲的儿子？哪个表示“很快”？太简单了。

cues.en: There's something else to learn from this quiet scribe. He's using radicals to clean up some ambiguity,
cues.zh: 从这位安静的抄写员身上，还能学到另一点。他在用部首消除一些歧义，

cues.en: but even he knows that context matters.
cues.zh: 但连他也知道，语境很重要。

cues.en: He won't spell everything out for you every time.
cues.zh: 他不会每次都把一切给你讲清楚。

cues.en: Sometimes this character means for,
cues.zh: 有时这个字表示“为了”，

cues.en: as in this is for you.
cues.zh: 就像“这是给你的”。

cues.en: Other times, it's the verb supply.
cues.zh: 另一些时候，它是动词“供给”。

cues.en: He's balancing this tension in the history of writing between what's easy on the reader, who needs more information to interpret the words, versus what's easy on the writer, who typically knows what he means when he's writing it, plus
cues.zh: 他在文字史中平衡着这种张力：一边是方便读者——读者需要更多信息来理解文字；另一边是方便写作者——写作者通常知道自己写的时候是什么意思，再加上

cues.en: hand cramps.
cues.zh: 手抽筋。

cues.en: The choice of leaving in or leaving out helpful information isn't simply about clarity and laziness,
cues.zh: 决定保留还是省略有用信息，不只是为了清晰或偷懒，

cues.en: it's aesthetic.
cues.zh: 也是审美问题。

cues.en: Throughout the history of Chinese calligraphy, from oracle moans to the rough cursive script, stylistic choices are made, not just semantic and phonetic choices.
cues.zh: 纵观中国书法史，从甲骨文到粗犷的草书，人们会做出风格上的选择，而不只是语义和语音上的选择。

cues.en: Seeing through the calligrapher's eyes, you can find in the history of writing not only a vision of what words and sounds look like, but where words and sounds go and where they stop.
cues.zh: 透过书法家的眼睛，你在书写史中不仅能看到词语和声音长什么样的图景，还能看到词语和声音去向何处、止于何处。

cues.en: When
cues.zh: 当

cues.en: it comes to aesthetic choices and Han characters, none is more fundamental than the decision to arrange character components in blocks.
cues.zh: 谈到审美选择和汉字时，没有什么比把字符部件排列成方块更根本的决定。

cues.en: Bonus note, this is definitely not the only time in history that writing gets organized in blocks.
cues.zh: 补充一点，这绝对不是历史上唯一一次文字被组织成方块。

cues.en: So this radical sits on top of this phonetic component in a block, making up one whole character, the character for flower. The ideograph man plus tree, a man leaning against a tree, has two components sitting side by side in a block, and they're the character for rest. And here's one tree in its own block, two trees meaning woods and three trees for forest.
cues.zh: 所以这个部首在一个方块里位于这个声旁之上，组成一个完整的汉字——花字。会意字“人”加“木”，即一个人靠在树上，两个部件在一个方块里并排，组成“休”字。这里是一棵树单独占一个方块，两棵树表示“林”，三棵树表示“森”。

cues.en: Aesthetics aside, what would happen if we took this sounds like principle a step further and made writing about the sounds?
cues.zh: 抛开美学不谈，如果我们把这个“听起来像”的原则再推进一步，让书写围绕声音来展开，会发生什么？

cues.en: Isn't that a better solution to our soon sun, sewn sun problem,
cues.zh: 这不正是解决我们“soon sun、sewn sun”这类问题更好的办法吗，

cues.en: and one that doesn't make us memorize tons of characters?
cues.zh: 而且不用让我们记住一大堆字符？

cues.en: A Maya stoneworker etches elaborate rows of characters onto a stela, a tall stone brought in from far away that's now standing straight up in the middle of the city. The characters he's carving look more like detailed pictures than writing, but don't let that fool you. Take a look at this block. It means mountain, but it's not a logograph standing for mountain.
cues.zh: 一位玛雅石匠在一块石碑上刻出一排排繁复的字符。这块高大的石头是从远方运来的，如今直立在城市中央。他刻的字符看起来更像精细的图画，而不是文字，但别被这一点骗了。看看这个字符块。它的意思是“山”，但它并不是一个表示“山”的表意文字。

cues.en: It's not a rebus symbol for think of a word that rhymes with shmountain.
cues.zh: 它不是那种让你联想一个和 shmountain 押韵的词的字谜符号。

cues.en: It's actually a block of two sound symbols that spell the word, wheatz, the Maya word for mountain.
cues.zh: 它其实是由两个表音符号组成的组合，拼出 wheatz 这个词，也就是玛雅语里的“山”。

cues.en: That's great for climbers, but chocolate lovers may instead prefer to sample these three symbols that together spell the word cacao,
cues.zh: 这对登山者很友好，但巧克力爱好者可能更想试试这三个符号，它们合起来拼出 cacao 这个词，

cues.en: cocoa. There's a nifty shortcut here. This bit doesn't even mean ka.
cues.zh: cocoa。这里有个很妙的捷径。这一小部分甚至并不表示 ka。

cues.en: It's actually a syllable multiplier
cues.zh: 它其实是一个音节重复符

cues.en: or iteration mark if you want the fancy name.
cues.zh: 或者如果你想用更花哨的叫法，就是迭代标记。

cues.en: Shh.
cues.zh: 嘘。

cues.en: I think you're being watched.
cues.zh: 我觉得有人在盯着你。

cues.en: Over there.
cues.zh: 就在那边。

cues.en: In the jungle?
cues.zh: 在丛林里？

cues.en: Maybe not.
cues.zh: 也许不是。

cues.en: Major moments in the history of writing.
cues.zh: 书写史上的重大时刻。

cues.en: Both of these Maya glyphs combine syllable characters into blocks to write words.
cues.zh: 这两个玛雅字符都把音节字符组合成方块来书写词语。

cues.en: This is full fledged sound writing.
cues.zh: 这是完全成熟的表音书写。

cues.en: These aren't logographs that happen to be read as sounds,
cues.zh: 它们不是恰好被读作声音的语标文字，

cues.en: they are sounds,
cues.zh: 它们就是声音，

cues.en: sounds capable of writing any syllable in the language.
cues.zh: 能够书写这门语言中任何音节的声音。

cues.en: In a full syllabary, like the classical Maya script, there are separate characters for just about every possible syllable in the language. No longer must you invent new word characters,
cues.zh: 在完整的音节文字体系中，比如古典玛雅文字，几乎语言中每个可能的音节都有单独的字符。你不再需要发明新的词字符，

cues.en: you can make do with a much smaller set of syllable characters.
cues.zh: 用一套小得多的音节字符就够了。

cues.en: Nice.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: But syllable writing comes with its own set of problems.
cues.zh: 但音节文字也有它自己的一系列问题。

cues.en: Here's a glyph that's quite useful around these parts.
cues.zh: 这里有个字形在这一带相当有用。

cues.en: Jaguar.
cues.zh: 美洲豹。

cues.en: The word is actually balam.
cues.zh: 这个词其实是 balam。

cues.en: But have you noticed something about the Mayan syllabary?
cues.zh: 但你注意到玛雅音节文字的特点了吗？

cues.en: Consonant plus vowel, consonant plus vowel,
cues.zh: 辅音加元音，辅音加元音，

cues.en: more consonants plus more vowels.
cues.zh: 更多辅音加更多元音。

cues.en: All of these syllables end in vowels.
cues.zh: 这些音节都以元音结尾。

cues.en: How in the world are you supposed to write the lam in balam?
cues.zh: 那到底该怎么写 balam 里的 lam 呢？

cues.en: Shifty, scripty syllabaries have grappled with this problem and settled on two solutions.
cues.zh: 那些多变又繁复的音节文字系统都设法解决过这个问题，最终定下了两种方案。

cues.en: One,
cues.zh: 第一种，

cues.en: leave out the final letter. Just
cues.zh: 省掉最后一个字母。直接

cues.en: ignore it. The term for this is underspelling
cues.zh: 无视它。这个术语叫少拼

cues.en: because you're not fully spelling the word, and it's a good solution because, you know, ignoring your problems makes them go away.
cues.zh: 因为你没有把单词完整拼出来，而且这是个好办法，因为你知道，无视问题，问题就会消失。

cues.en: Option two.
cues.zh: 第二种。

cues.en: Spell the last letter with an extra syllable,
cues.zh: 给最后一个字母多拼一个音节，

cues.en: but use a syllable that just repeats the last vowel so that we know we can just ignore the final vowel.
cues.zh: 但要用一个只重复最后一个元音的音节，这样我们就知道可以直接忽略末尾的元音。

cues.en: This gets called the echo vowel.
cues.zh: 这叫做回声元音。

cues.en: Mayan likes number two
cues.zh: 玛雅人喜欢数字二

cues.en: a lot.
cues.zh: 非常喜欢。

cues.en: So cacao is ka ka wa. Well,
cues.zh: 所以 cacao 就是 ka ka wa。嗯，

cues.en: ka times two wa.
cues.zh: ka 乘二，wa。

cues.en: Witz,
cues.zh: Witz，

cues.en: the mountain, is actually Witzi.
cues.zh: 这座山，其实是 Witzi。

cues.en: And your new pet Balam is spelled Balama.
cues.zh: 而你的新宠物 Balam 拼作 Balama。

cues.en: Cross out the echo vowels, and the words practically read themselves.
cues.zh: 划掉回声元音，这些词几乎自己就能读出来。

cues.en: Your new friend pulls you along to show you another project he's working on, an Amate Codex. That's a paper book.
cues.zh: 你的新朋友拉着你去看他正在做的另一个项目——一本 Amate Codex。那是一本纸质书。

cues.en: Yes. He has paper and, yes, books.
cues.zh: 是的。他有纸，而且，没错，还有书。

cues.en: But that's not what's got him excited.
cues.zh: 但让他兴奋的并不是这个。

cues.en: He folds open the book he's working on, maybe to share new ideas?
cues.zh: 他翻开正在写的书，也许是想分享新想法？

cues.en: No.
cues.zh: 不。

cues.en: To brag about how inventive and potentially efficient his writing system is? No.
cues.zh: 想炫耀他的书写系统多有创意、可能多高效？不。

cues.en: For his people, the invention of the new wasn't about ditching the old.
cues.zh: 对他的族人来说，发明新东西并不是要抛弃旧的。

cues.en: He shows you how creative he's been with the characters you learned. He shows you a mountain and calls it Vietz,
cues.zh: 他向你展示，他用你学过的字符玩出了多少创意。他指着一座山，叫它 Vietz，

cues.en: and then a jaguar and calls it Balam.
cues.zh: 然后指着一只美洲豹，叫它 Balam。

cues.en: Logographs?
cues.zh: 表意文字？

cues.en: Wait a second. You stop and ask him, which is the correct way to write Balam?
cues.zh: 等等。你停下来问他，Balam 到底该怎么写才对？

cues.en: He writes Balama.
cues.zh: 他写 Balama。

cues.en: You ask him to write it again, and he writes the logograph,
cues.zh: 你让他再写一遍，他写了个词符，

cues.en: but with a syllable. And again, but he writes the logograph plus two syllables.
cues.zh: 但带一个音节。再来一遍，他写词符加两个音节。

cues.en: He smiles mischievously.
cues.zh: 他调皮地笑了笑。

cues.en: They're all balam.
cues.zh: 它们都是 balam。

cues.en: This is what he's proud of. He can write the same word, even the same syllable, in different ways and combinations without repeating himself.
cues.zh: 这是他引以为豪的。同一个词，甚至同一个音节，他都能用不同方式和组合写出来，而不重复自己。

cues.en: Creative.
cues.zh: 有创意。

cues.en: But his use of logographs plus syllables recalls the tension between sound writing and meaning writing.
cues.zh: 但他把词符和音节结合使用，让人想起表音文字与表意文字之间的张力。

cues.en: Meaningful determinatives helped us choose the right pronunciation for our rebus character, and Mayan logographs can still do that. But the helping hand goes both ways.
cues.zh: 有意义的限定符帮我们为画谜字符选对了读音，玛雅意符至今也能做到这一点。但这种帮助是双向的。

cues.en: The syllabary can also clarify the sounds you should make when you read a logograph.
cues.zh: 音节表也能说明你读一个意符时该发什么音。

cues.en: Here's the character jaguar,
cues.zh: 这是“美洲豹”字符，

cues.en: but add a couple extra syllable hints and you make it clear that we're meant to read this glyph as balama minus
cues.zh: 但再加上几个音节提示，就能明确：这个字形要读作 balama 减去

cues.en: the echo vowel, so balam.
cues.zh: 回声元音，也就是 balam。

cues.en: These are phonetic complements,
cues.zh: 这些是表音补足成分，

cues.en: pronunciation clues sitting comfortably alongside logographs.
cues.zh: 是自然伴随在意符旁边的发音线索。

cues.en: If that's all too complex,
cues.zh: 如果这太复杂，

cues.en: just remember that you can write everything in syllables.
cues.zh: 只需记住，一切都可以用音节写出来。

cues.en: But before you have time to settle into this land of balam and cacao to practice those syllables,
cues.zh: 可还没等你适应这片美洲豹与可可之地、开始练习这些音节，

cues.en: a sandy wind starts blowing in from the east. A familiar reminder from a faraway land where even more dramatic changes are about to shape the future of writing.
cues.zh: 一阵沙尘风便从东方吹来。那是来自遥远国度的熟悉提醒——在那里，更剧烈的变化即将塑造文字的未来。

cues.en: Even in these ancient times, Egyptian monuments have been sitting and weathering for thousands of years.
cues.zh: 即使在那个远古时代，埃及遗迹也已经矗立并风化了几千年。

cues.en: On their great murals and pillars, you find rows of little pictures.
cues.zh: 在它们巨大的壁画和石柱上，你会看到一排排小图画。

cues.en: Sorry, not pictures.
cues.zh: 抱歉，不是图画。

cues.en: Hieroglyphs,
cues.zh: 是圣书字，

cues.en: sacred symbols.
cues.zh: 神圣符号。

cues.en: But despite appearances, this isn't some mysterious pharaonic picture writing.
cues.zh: 但别看表面，这并不是什么神秘的法老图画文字。

cues.en: It's consonants.
cues.zh: 这是辅音。

cues.en: One consonant signs,
cues.zh: 单辅音符号，

cues.en: two consonant signs,
cues.zh: 双辅音符号，

cues.en: three consonant signs, a wall of consonants,
cues.zh: 三辅音符号，一整墙的辅音，

cues.en: plus a sprinkle of logographs for determinatives.
cues.zh: 再加上零星的表意符号作限定符。

cues.en: It's not that Egyptian was a harsh voweless desert of a tongue. It simply did not write its vowels.
cues.zh: 倒不是说古埃及语是一门严酷、没有元音的荒漠式语言；它只是不把元音写出来。

cues.en: Imagine if you wrote this way.
cues.zh: 想象一下，你要是这么写会怎样。

cues.en: Would that work? And then imagine if you could add in logographs to make sure you really got your point across.
cues.zh: 这行得通吗？再想象一下，你还能加入表意符号，确保真正把意思传达清楚。

cues.en: Imagine you wrote like that, and you're thinking with hieroglyphs.
cues.zh: 想象你那样书写，用象形文字来思考。

cues.en: Too difficult?
cues.zh: 太难了？

cues.en: Fine.
cues.zh: 好吧。

cues.en: Off to the caves with you, where you toil away with ancient miners on the Sinai Peninsula.
cues.zh: 那你就去洞穴里吧，在西奈半岛和古代矿工一起辛苦劳作。

cues.en: You and your fellow miners would find it handy to leave messages for one another, but there's no time for deep studies of rows of fancy hieroglyphs in here. You need to keep it simple if you want another.
cues.zh: 你和同伴矿工们会发现，互相留消息很方便，但在这里没时间深入研究一排排花哨的象形文字。想再收到一条消息，就得写得简单。

cues.en: Major moments in the history of writing.
cues.zh: 书写史上的重大时刻。

cues.en: Your characters look like scratchy, rushed version of those glamorous Egyptian symbols,
cues.zh: 你的字符看起来像那些华丽埃及符号的潦草、匆忙版本，

cues.en: but their meaning doesn't matter anymore.
cues.zh: 但它们的意思已经不重要了。

cues.en: Nothing but consonants,
cues.zh: 只有辅音，

cues.en: and the same symbol for the same consonant
cues.zh: 而且同一个辅音用同一个符号

cues.en: every time.
cues.zh: 每次都一样。

cues.en: Take this character.
cues.zh: 拿这个字符来说。

cues.en: In Egyptian, it means house. The Semitic miners are calling a house a bet.
cues.zh: 在埃及语里，它表示房子。闪米特矿工把房子叫作 bet。

cues.en: Acrophony
cues.zh: 首音法

cues.en: or top sounds suggest that you can just take the first letter of a word like the Egyptians had already been doing with much of their consonant writing.
cues.zh: 也就是取词首音，意味着你可以直接取一个词的首字母，就像埃及人已经在很多辅音书写中做的那样。

cues.en: You end up with a letter for your sound b.
cues.zh: 你就得到了表示 b 音的字母。

cues.en: Do the same thing with water, which the Semitic speakers are calling mem, and you now have an m sound.
cues.zh: 对水也做同样的事，闪米特语使用者把它叫作 mem，你就有了 m 音。

cues.en: With a couple dozen elegant simplifications,
cues.zh: 经过几十处优雅的简化，

cues.en: you create a simple, reliable list of consonants,
cues.zh: 你创建出一份简单、可靠的辅音表，

cues.en: an alphabet,
cues.zh: 一套字母表，

cues.en: and you've given generations of future children the joys of reciting their a b c's.
cues.zh: 也让未来一代代孩子享受到背诵 a b c 的乐趣。

cues.en: Actually, at this point in history, they're a b g d's,
cues.zh: 其实，到了历史上这个节点，它们就是 a、b、g、d，

cues.en: sometimes called an abjad or abgog,
cues.zh: 有时被称为 abjad 或 abgog，

cues.en: because who needs that wishy washy c when you can just use an s or a k?
cues.zh: 既然能用 s 或 k，谁还需要那个模棱两可的 c 呢？

cues.en: After a long hard day of mining and etching,
cues.zh: 辛苦采矿和蚀刻一整天后，

cues.en: you turn to find that someone's been watching you this whole time.
cues.zh: 你转过身，发现有人一直在看着你。

cues.en: She's a traitor,
cues.zh: 她是个叛徒，

cues.en: a Phoenician merchant who knows a good thing when she sees it. She's already made major cash in the paper business, where they turn tufty, stocky, swampy Egyptian papyrus
cues.zh: 一个腓尼基商人，一眼就能看出好东西。她已经在纸业赚了大钱——人们把一丛丛、粗壮、湿软的埃及纸莎草

cues.en: into flat inkable sheets of paper.
cues.zh: 变成平整、可书写的纸张。

cues.en: She rushes back home to Phoenicia and smirks.
cues.zh: 她赶回腓尼基的家，得意地一笑。

cues.en: Think of the advantage she has, keeping track of whatever anyone else tells her just by remembering about as many characters as she has fingers and toes.
cues.zh: 想想她的优势：只需记住和手指脚趾总数差不多多的字母，就能把别人告诉她的任何事都记下来。

cues.en: Old kings can keep their obtuse hieroglyphs and their stone monuments.
cues.zh: 旧日的国王们尽可以守着他那晦涩的象形文字和石头纪念碑。

cues.en: The future of the Mediterranean will belong to alphabets and paper.
cues.zh: 地中海的未来将属于字母表和纸。

cues.en: Writing is going portable.
cues.zh: 书写正在变得便携。

cues.en: She uses this newfound alphabetic leverage to turn a huge profit across the entire Eastern Mediterranean,
cues.zh: 她利用这种新得的字母优势，在整个东地中海赚得盆满钵满，

cues.en: leaving people inspired to adopt and adapt her alphabet wherever she goes. All this, and she doesn't even write you a thank you card? How hard could it be? Writing is easier than ever.
cues.zh: 无论走到哪里，都让人们深受启发，去采用并改造她的字母表。做了这么多，她居然连张感谢卡都不给你写？这能有多难？书写已经比以往任何时候都容易。

cues.en: It feels universal,
cues.zh: 这感觉像是普世的，

cues.en: like writing's here to stay for everyone.
cues.zh: 仿佛文字会永远陪伴所有人。

cues.en: But there's a peculiar quirk that's easier to spot in hindsight.
cues.zh: 但有个奇怪的蹊跷之处，事后回看更容易发现。

cues.en: You and your mining crew were communicating in a Semitic language.
cues.zh: 你和你的采矿队用的是某种闪米特语交流。

cues.en: Phoenicians are Semitic language.
cues.zh: 腓尼基人用的是闪米特语。

cues.en: All of these friendly shades of the Phoenician alphabet were being used for languages that sounded similar and worked much the same way.
cues.zh: 腓尼基字母表这些亲切的变体，都被用来书写发音相近、运作方式也大同小异的语言。

cues.en: Even Egyptian, though no Semitic language itself,
cues.zh: 就连埃及语，虽然它本身不属于闪米特语，

cues.en: is at least a distant relative of the Semitic languages with a similar personality.
cues.zh: 至少也是闪米特诸语的远亲，脾气还挺像。

cues.en: This consonant alphabet is being tested in easy waters,
cues.zh: 这套辅音字母表正在平静的水域接受测试，

cues.en: but history is shaking things up. Your merchant friend comes back for your help. She needs you to deliver your alphabet to a very different people living along her trade route.
cues.zh: 但历史正在搅动局面。你的商人朋友回来找你帮忙。她需要你把你的字母表送给她商路上一个截然不同的族群。

cues.en: What will happen when the alphabet gets leaked outside of the family?
cues.zh: 当字母表泄露到家族之外，会发生什么？

cues.en: Greece.
cues.zh: 希腊。

cues.en: No, not that Greece.
cues.zh: 不，不是那个希腊。

cues.en: Greece before there was a Parthenon.
cues.zh: 帕特农神庙尚未建成时的希腊。

cues.en: A stern old man in a trademark sporty toga seems a bit on edge as he glares at the papyrus sheet clutched in his hand. You see?
cues.zh: 一个身穿标志性运动风托加袍的严厉老人，正怒视着手里攥着的莎草纸，看起来有点紧张。看到了吗？

cues.en: You try to shrug off his outburst,
cues.zh: 你想对他的情绪爆发不以为意，

cues.en: but he can't let this go. My friend, my friend.
cues.zh: 但他放不下这件事。我的朋友啊，我的朋友。

cues.en: He recounts how five hundred years before he was even born, when the walls of Troy still stood, the Greeks had a writing system of their own.
cues.zh: 他讲述道，在他出生前五百年、特洛伊城墙尚在时，希腊人就已有自己的文字系统。

cues.en: It was one of those more elaborate syllabary plus logograph types.
cues.zh: 那属于更繁复的音节文字加表意文字类型。

cues.en: But that script had come, and it had gone.
cues.zh: 但那种文字来了，又消失了。

cues.en: The new Greeks were a people on the rise, but an illiterate people on the rise.
cues.zh: 新的希腊人是崛起中的民族，但也是崛起中的文盲民族。

cues.en: A people looking for something new, something great,
cues.zh: 一个民族在寻找某种新事物，某种伟大的事物，

cues.en: and this alphabet thing seems great,
cues.zh: 而这个字母系统看起来很棒，

cues.en: almost.
cues.zh: 差不多吧。

cues.en: He calls over his close friends.
cues.zh: 他把好友们叫了过来。

cues.en: The Phoenician consonants are useful, he concedes, but why these extra characters for huffing, coughing, and clearing
cues.zh: 他承认腓尼基语的辅音很有用，但为什么要多出这些字符，用来喘气、咳嗽、清

cues.en: your throat?
cues.zh: 嗓子？

cues.en: These are barbarian
cues.zh: 这些是野蛮人的

cues.en: sounds.
cues.zh: 声音。

cues.en: Greeks have no need for them. And what about the voicy noises like ah and oh?
cues.zh: 希腊人不需要它们。那像“啊”和“哦”这样的元音呢？

cues.en: How to write them, So
cues.zh: 怎么把它们写出来，多出

cues.en: much extra yet so much missing. What a mess.
cues.zh: 这么多，却缺了这么多。真是一团糟。

cues.en: You try to explain, but they laugh it off.
cues.zh: 你想解释，却被他们一笑置之。

cues.en: Here, I I fix for you, he says.
cues.zh: “来，我帮你改好，”他说。

cues.en: See, he was going to ditch the, mhmm, barbarian letters,
cues.zh: 你看，他本来打算丢掉那些，嗯，蛮族的字母，

cues.en: but he had second thoughts and it struck him. Why not use these on Greek sounds for vowels?
cues.zh: 但他转念一想，忽然有了主意：何不把这些字母用来表示希腊语里的元音？

cues.en: The one you call Aleph,
cues.zh: 你们称作 Aleph 的那个字母，

cues.en: ignore the throaty catch at the beginning. It's ah.
cues.zh: 别管开头那个喉咙里的卡顿，它是 ah。

cues.en: Take that he, but ditch the h, and we're left with a vowel y e.
cues.zh: 拿那个 he，去掉 h，就剩下元音 e。

cues.en: Loosen up that tight w in wow,
cues.zh: 把 wow 里那个紧绷的 w 放松，

cues.en: and it's the vowel u.
cues.zh: 就成了元音 u。

cues.en: This isn't just a small correction.
cues.zh: 这可不只是一次小小的修正。

cues.en: This is a powerful Major moments in the history of writing.
cues.zh: 这是书写史上一个影响深远的重大时刻。

cues.en: He's fundamentally shifted the way the alphabet functions.
cues.zh: 他从根本上改变了字母表的运作方式。

cues.en: It used to be just the consonant suggesting the pronunciation of a word. Once you recognize the word, the job's done. But Greek spelling isn't merely about writing recognizable words. It's about matching letters to sounds.
cues.zh: 过去，辅音只是提示一个词的发音。一旦你认出这个词，任务就完成了。但希腊语拼写不只在于写出可识别的词，而在于让字母与声音相匹配。

cues.en: A new principle has just emerged,
cues.zh: 一个新的原则刚刚出现，

cues.en: perhaps even a new goal, one sound,
cues.zh: 甚至可能是一个新目标：一个音，

cues.en: one character.
cues.zh: 一个字符。

cues.en: You suspect that he's not even aware of the impact of his discovery as he tells you to drop everything and come enjoy some dinner and dancing.
cues.zh: 你猜他根本没意识到自己的发现有多大影响，还叫你放下一切去吃饭跳舞。

cues.en: You silly.
cues.zh: 你这个小傻瓜。

cues.en: The party goes on and on, so long that your new friends don't even see what's happening beyond the walls of their city state. This consonant vowel alphabet,
cues.zh: 派对一直开个不停，久到你的新朋友根本看不到他们城邦墙外正在发生什么。这套辅音元音字母表，

cues.en: this pronunciation writing is spreading,
cues.zh: 这种表音文字正在传播，

cues.en: inspiring new alphabets to the East, with flavors like Armenian and Cyrillic popping up. Out west in Italy, the Tuscans,
cues.zh: 启发东方诞生新的字母表，亚美尼亚字母和西里尔字母等纷纷冒出来。向西到意大利，托斯卡纳人，

cues.en: the Etruscans borrow it, and they pass it on to the Romans.
cues.zh: 伊特鲁里亚人借用了它，又把它传给罗马人。

cues.en: The Romans burst out and splatter it among the Celts and Germanic peoples,
cues.zh: 罗马人冲了出来，把它传播给凯尔特人和日耳曼人，

cues.en: and eventually the world.
cues.zh: 最终传遍世界。

cues.en: Such a visual rainbow of variations,
cues.zh: 如此五彩斑斓的变体，

cues.en: and yet they'll all stick with the basic principle of writing a character for each sound, consonants,
cues.zh: 但它们都坚持基本原则：每个音写一个字符——辅音，

cues.en: and vowels.
cues.zh: 和元音。

cues.en: Finally,
cues.zh: 最后，

cues.en: you see your writing system in this story, your alphabet,
cues.zh: 你在这段故事里看到了你的书写系统，你的字母表，

cues.en: all because a handful of Semitic symbols got mistaken for Greek vowels.
cues.zh: 全因为几个闪米特符号被误认成了希腊元音。

cues.en: But before you get overconfident,
cues.zh: 但别太早自信，

cues.en: know that the history of writing doesn't stop here.
cues.zh: 要知道，书写的历史并未止步于此。

cues.en: This isn't the be all and end all, not even close.
cues.zh: 这还不是全部，差得远呢。

cues.en: You're back in old Phoenicia,
cues.zh: 你又回到了古老的腓尼基，

cues.en: where it turns out the Greeks aren't the only ones looking to buy a vowel.
cues.zh: 结果发现，想买元音的并不只有希腊人。

cues.en: Your contact in town is still your merchant frenemy who reminds you of how she traded your consonant alphabet across the ancient world.
cues.zh: 你在城里的联络人还是那位亦敌亦友的商人，她提醒你，她当年如何把你这套辅音字母表卖遍古代世界。

cues.en: That abjad spread to every language with even a passing resemblance to Phoenician.
cues.zh: 这套辅音字母系统传到了每一种哪怕只是略微像腓尼基语的语言。

cues.en: Every town from here to Carthage has some version of her Abjad.
cues.zh: 从这里到迦太基，每座城镇都有她那套辅音字母系统的某个版本。

cues.en: Spot the Egyptians, those stuck in their way traditionalists.
cues.zh: 看看埃及人，那些固守传统、墨守成规的人。

cues.en: Initially, these Semitic speakers loved it. They were proud of it. But the days are turning to years, and that love grows cold.
cues.zh: 起初，这些闪米特语使用者很喜欢它。他们为它感到自豪。但日子变成了一年又一年，那份爱渐渐冷淡。

cues.en: They grumble that they're stuck with these consonants,
cues.zh: 他们抱怨自己只能守着这些辅音，

cues.en: just consonants.
cues.zh: 只有辅音。

cues.en: Clamoring for vowels, they get desperate and grab a few characters to stand in for a long sound.
cues.zh: 他们渴求元音，情急之下抓来几个字符，用来代表一个长音。

cues.en: Take a look. This symbol is originally the stop between a a a. This one's a y, a you sound.
cues.zh: 看一看。这个符号原本是 a a a 之间的停顿。这个是 y，是 you 的音。

cues.en: And this is a wa.
cues.zh: 这就是 wa。

cues.en: But they're about to become not these things, thanks to... Major moments in the history of writing.
cues.zh: 但它们即将不再是这些东西，多亏了……书写史上的重大时刻。

cues.en: This moment hits you twice because it brings up both an innovation specific to Semitic scripts and a more general principle that kind of bends the rules of the alphabet game. First, it's worth reiterating that Abjad writing systems are viable ways to write and read a language.
cues.zh: 这一刻会给你双重冲击，因为它既涉及闪米特文字特有的创新，也涉及一个更普遍的原则——某种程度上打破了字母游戏的规则。首先值得重申：Abjad 书写系统是可行书写和阅读语言的方式。

cues.en: They work. But with one obvious shortcoming,
cues.zh: 它们确实管用。但有一个明显的缺点，

cues.en: those missing vowels can create ambiguous situations.
cues.zh: 那些缺失的元音会造成歧义。

cues.en: But what if, instead of writing every vowel, we just had a few helpful hinters that suggested the presence of certain kinds of vowels?
cues.zh: 但如果我们不写出每个元音，而是只用几个有用的提示符来暗示某类元音的存在，会怎样？

cues.en: Take this letter, w. Actually, they called it wow. Wow.
cues.zh: 拿这个字母 w 来说。其实，他们把它叫作 wow。Wow。

cues.en: Now imagine that we keep using it in words that have the sound w,
cues.zh: 现在想象我们继续在含有 w 音的词里使用它，

cues.en: but we also extend its use, placing it between consonants for the similar enough vowel sound, u. In the old Abjad, you'd have to write soon and sun with the same characters, s plus n. Everything else is vowels and we don't have those. But suddenly, our extended w comes in handy.
cues.zh: 但我们也扩展它的用法，把它放在辅音之间，来表示足够接近的元音 u。在古老的 Abjad 中，你得用同样的字符 s 加 n 来写 soon 和 sun。其余都是元音，而我们没有这些。但突然间，我们扩展后的 w 就派上用场了。

cues.en: Sun doesn't have that oo sound, so it's still s plus n.
cues.zh: Sun 里没有那个 oo 音，所以仍然是 s 加 n。

cues.en: But sun does, so we add in the w.
cues.zh: 但 sun 有，所以要补上 w。

cues.en: Do the same thing with you, which can double as a long I,
cues.zh: 对 you 也照做，它还能兼作长音 I，

cues.en: and this quirky catch in your throat pause between uh-oh,
cues.zh: 还有这个古怪的喉部卡顿，就在 uh-oh 之间，

cues.en: alef,
cues.zh: alef，

cues.en: which can double as a long ah,
cues.zh: 它可以兼作长音 ah，

cues.en: and you end up with three handy vowel suggestors,
cues.zh: 最后你就有了三个顺手的元音提示符，

cues.en: the matres lektionis.
cues.zh: 也就是 matres lektionis。

cues.en: These helpful mothers of reading that show up in Aramaic,
cues.zh: 这些帮助阅读的母亲，出现在阿拉姆语、

cues.en: Hebrew, Arabic, and Syriac.
cues.zh: 希伯来语、阿拉伯语和叙利亚语中。

cues.en: But these mothers don't leave their consonantness behind.
cues.zh: 但这些母亲并没有丢掉自己的辅音性。

cues.en: They still double as consonants.
cues.zh: 它们仍兼作辅音。

cues.en: The Abjad traded the ambiguity of a vowel less existence for new kind of ambiguity.
cues.zh: 辅音音素文字用无元音的歧义，换来了新的歧义。

cues.en: Depending on context, each of these matres may be a consonant or it might be a vowel.
cues.zh: 视上下文而定，这些 matres 每一个都可能是辅音，也可能是元音。

cues.en: One character,
cues.zh: 一个字符，

cues.en: multiple sounds.
cues.zh: 多种发音。

cues.en: This is a huge trend in alphabets.
cues.zh: 这是字母文字中的一大趋势。

cues.en: Why invent new characters when you can reuse an old one?
cues.zh: 能复用旧字符，何必发明新字符？

cues.en: Repurposing consonants for vowels here and there won't satisfy everyone.
cues.zh: 零星地把辅音改作元音，并不能让所有人满意。

cues.en: These bickering scribes aren't content with matres lektiones.
cues.zh: 这些争吵不休的抄写员并不满足于 matres lektiones。

cues.en: They're not just trying to tell sun apart from sun. The bickering scribes are bickering over how to read one of their most treasured sayings.
cues.zh: 他们不只是想分清太阳和太阳。争吵的抄写员们正在为如何解读他们最珍视的一句格言而争吵。

cues.en: One says that it's such a fine point, you wouldn't understand unless you were incredibly well versed in his language.
cues.zh: 一个人说，这一点太微妙了，除非你对他的语言极为精通，否则根本不会懂。

cues.en: But he makes an analogy for you. Write the word news in a consonant only alphabet. It's n w s. Fine. Now imagine that someone comes along with their fancy consonant vowel hybrids and spells the word noose,
cues.zh: 但他给你打了个比方。用只有辅音的字母表写出 news 这个词，就是 n w s。好。现在想象有人带着他们花哨的辅音-元音混合字母出现，把 noose 这个词拼成，

cues.en: n w s.
cues.zh: n w s。

cues.en: Wait
cues.zh: 稍等

cues.en: a second.
cues.zh: 一下。

cues.en: He shows you a cheat sheet he's been keeping. It's so easy, he says, pointing out the little dots and dashes above and below letters to keep his vowel straight. Put them here for an a, there for an a. You can even add them below one of the long vowel things if you need to distinguish, say, an e. Nobody's confused.
cues.zh: 他给你看了一张自己一直留着的小抄。他说这特别简单，一边指着字母上下的小点和短横，说这是为了让元音不混淆。a 的就放这儿，a 的就放那儿。要是需要区分，比如 e，你甚至可以把它们加在某个长元音符号下面。没人会搞混。

cues.en: That's it. He won't tolerate the vagueness any longer.
cues.zh: 够了。他再也不会容忍这种含糊不清。

cues.en: Effective immediately in all important texts where clear reading matters, everyone should use this method.
cues.zh: 立即生效：在所有需要清晰阅读的重要文本中，大家都应使用这种方法。

cues.en: And so for generations, scribes would mark vowels above and below the consonants, writing vowels in what was once a consonant only alphabet.
cues.zh: 于是世代以来，抄写员会在辅音上方和下方标出元音，把元音写进原本只有辅音的字母表。

cues.en: But as much as the pious and students swear by their dotty vowels,
cues.zh: 但尽管虔诚者和学生都笃信这些带点的元音，

cues.en: modern Arabic and Hebrew speakers stick with the simple consonants plus the extended consonant vowel mothers. The optional helper dots get thrown in like a life preserver for struggling learners or careful text.
cues.zh: 现代阿拉伯语和希伯来语使用者仍坚持使用简单的辅音，再加上扩展的“元音母”辅音。可选的辅助点号则像救生圈一样，被抛给吃力的学习者或需要严谨处理的文本。

cues.en: But grown ups don't need them anymore.
cues.zh: 但成年人不再需要它们了。

cues.en: Man, let's take you.
cues.zh: 老兄，我们带你去吧。

cues.en: A spice market in India.
cues.zh: 印度的一个香料市场。

cues.en: The hooded figure in front of you apologizes for the kidnapping.
cues.zh: 你面前那个戴兜帽的人为这次绑架道歉。

cues.en: He needs your help. He explains that his land has taken part in history's most elaborate and rigorous memorization exercises.
cues.zh: 他需要你的帮助。他解释说，他的故土参与过历史上最复杂、最严苛的记忆训练。

cues.en: Instead of scribes, they had recitations.
cues.zh: 他们没有抄写员，而是靠背诵。

cues.en: These weren't retellings of campfire stories, these were whole libraries of knowledge handed down for generations.
cues.zh: 这些不是篝火故事的复述，而是代代相传的整座知识宝库。

cues.en: He says his name is Ashoka.
cues.zh: 他说自己叫 Ashoka。

cues.en: This is his land and he is king.
cues.zh: 这是他的土地，他是国王。

cues.en: After a bloody and violent war, he had a change of heart and now has but one singular focus,
cues.zh: 经历一场血腥暴力的战争后，他改变了心意，如今只有一个明确目标，

cues.en: to spread his message, a law of tolerance and compassion throughout the land.
cues.zh: 把自己的理念——一部宽容与慈悲之法——传遍整个国土。

cues.en: But he doesn't want to use the mouth to ear memorization ways of the oral tradition.
cues.zh: 但他不想用口耳相传、死记硬背的口述传统方式。

cues.en: That's for old texts and old ideas.
cues.zh: 那是留给旧文本和旧思想的。

cues.en: No. His vision is to install massive pillars around his empire,
cues.zh: 不。他的设想是在帝国各地竖立巨大的石柱，

cues.en: each one engraved with his list of edicts.
cues.zh: 每根都刻上他的敕令清单。

cues.en: This, he explains, is where you come in. See, he's been keeping tabs on you as you roam the land of the Semitic Abjads and he really likes this crazy consonant alphabet idea. He'll take it. But he also appreciates the whimsical simplicity of accenting consonants with vowel marks. Oh, and he doesn't wanna have to write the vowel if it's just a short
cues.zh: 他解释说，这正是你登场的地方。你看，当你在闪米特辅音文字的世界里游荡时，他一直在关注你，而且他真的很喜欢这个疯狂的辅音字母表点子。他会采纳它。但他也欣赏用元音符号标注辅音那种异想天开的简洁。哦，而且如果只是短元音，他不想非得把元音写出来

cues.en: His language is full of those. So he'll write funnel something like this with these built in syllables.
cues.zh: 他的语言里到处都是这种短元音。所以他会把 funnel 写成这样，带上这些内置音节。

cues.en: But wait, it's not funnel
cues.zh: 等等，这不是 funnel

cues.en: That final l isn't a separate syllable.
cues.zh: 词尾的 l 并不是单独的音节。

cues.en: He needs a way to write just bare consonants to tell his past apart from his pasta.
cues.zh: 他需要一种只写纯辅音的方法，好区分 past 和 pasta。

cues.en: How? With a simple hush stroke below the letter.
cues.zh: 怎么做？在字母下方加一道简单的静音笔画。

cues.en: Now, he brags to you, his system is complete.
cues.zh: 现在，他向你夸口：他的系统已经完整。

cues.en: Make sure you don't miss the step he's taking here. It's a major
cues.zh: 注意别错过他在这里迈出的一步。这是书写史上一个重大

cues.en: moments in the history of writing.
cues.zh: 时刻。

cues.en: Each of the character units fundamentally represents a syllable.
cues.zh: 每个字符单元本质上都代表一个音节。

cues.en: It just so happens that unless the vowel in that syllable is a short ah, the vowel gets added onto or below or beside the consonant character.
cues.zh: 只是说，除非那个音节里的元音是短音 ah，否则元音会加在辅音字符的上方、下方或旁边。

cues.en: On their own, the base characters contain that dummy vowel,
cues.zh: 单独看时，基础字符本身就含有那个占位元音，

cues.en: like p. But you can take that p and modify it with any vowel you like.
cues.zh: 比如 p。但你可以拿这个 p，用任意你想要的元音去修饰它。

cues.en: Certain vowels go in certain places, like e to the side or u below.
cues.zh: 某些元音会放在特定位置，比如 e 在侧面，u 在下方。

cues.en: So in India, characters are syllables.
cues.zh: 所以在印度，字符就是音节。

cues.en: But unlike a full syllabary, you don't need a completely separate character for each separate syllable.
cues.zh: 但与完整的音节文字不同，你不需要为每个单独的音节都用一个完全独立的字符。

cues.en: And all characters give consonant plus vowel information,
cues.zh: 而且所有字符都给出辅音加元音的信息，

cues.en: but unlike a full alphabet, you don't line up sequences of consonants plus vowels, consonants plus vowels.
cues.zh: 但和完整字母表不同，你不会把“辅音加元音、辅音加元音”这样依次排开。

cues.en: The hybrid combination nature of this system earns it the name alpha syllabary.
cues.zh: 这种混合组合的特性，让它得名“元音附标文字”。

cues.en: Combos are built into this system, paving the way for over a thousand ligatures,
cues.zh: 组合被内建在这套系统中，为上千个连字铺平了道路，

cues.en: commonly linked characters,
cues.zh: 也就是常见的连写字符，

cues.en: in the alpha syllabary.
cues.zh: 在这套元音附标文字里。

cues.en: Sure, other writing systems developed ligatures in their calligraphy,
cues.zh: 当然，其他书写系统也在书法中发展出了连字，

cues.en: but the Indic alpha syllabary welcomes them naturally.
cues.zh: 但印度系的元音附标文字天然就接纳它们。

cues.en: As it's passed all around this entire slice of the world, up to Nepal and Tibet, down the coast to Burma, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, and beyond, the script keeps updating its look but continues to capture consonants and vowels accurately, like an alphabet, and to write those voweled consonants in syllable units, like a syllabary.
cues.zh: 它传遍这一整片区域，向北到尼泊尔和西藏，沿海南下到缅甸、泰国、老挝、柬埔寨乃至更远；这种文字的外观不断演变，却仍像字母表那样准确记录辅音和元音，并像音节文字那样把带元音的辅音按音节单位书写。

cues.en: Even completely unrelated alpha syllabaries seize on this same idea.
cues.zh: 就连完全无关的字母音节文字也采用了同样的思路。

cues.en: This is the Ethiopic symbol for ma. This one reads me,
cues.zh: 这是埃塞俄比亚文字中表示 ma 的符号。这个读作 me，

cues.en: and this is mu.
cues.zh: 而这个是 mu。

cues.en: This is la, le, and lu. Now that you understand alpha syllabaries, you must answer this next question.
cues.zh: 这是 la、le 和 lu。既然你已经弄懂了元音附标文字，那接下来这个问题你必须回答。

cues.en: If this symbol sounds like ba,
cues.zh: 如果这个符号读作 ba，

cues.en: how do you write ba and bu in Ethiopia?
cues.zh: 在埃塞俄比亚，ba 和 bu 该怎么写？

cues.en: This is your Ge'ez a b c d's, the abugida.
cues.zh: 这是你的 Ge'ez 字母表，也就是 abugida 元音附标文字。

cues.en: Looks different, but works much the same way.
cues.zh: 看起来不一样，但运作方式大同小异。

cues.en: Your characters have never looked so different, even after the Greeks and Romans took them over. Maybe it's this dizzying variety of writing systems,
cues.zh: 你的字符从没显得这么不一样过，哪怕被希腊人和罗马人接手之后也是如此。也许是因为书写系统这种令人眼花缭乱的多样性，

cues.en: or maybe Thoth's pill is starting to wear off.
cues.zh: 又或者，托特的药丸开始失效了。

cues.en: Another time, another king,
cues.zh: 另一个时代，另一位国王，

cues.en: this time in a Korean palace. He presents himself as king Sejong.
cues.zh: 这一次是在一座朝鲜宫殿里。他自称世宗大王。

cues.en: As you get a grip on your surroundings, you begin to tell him of your journeys.
cues.zh: 当你逐渐弄清周围环境，你开始向他讲述你的旅程。

cues.en: Yet, with a sweeping gaze, the king looks right past you.
cues.zh: 然而，国王扫视一圈，目光却径直越过你。

cues.en: You've been out for a very long time,
cues.zh: 你已经沉睡了很久，

cues.en: over a thousand years.
cues.zh: 超过一千年。

cues.en: The world has come so far, and the scripts you once knew have too.
cues.zh: 世界已经发展至此，你曾经熟知的文字也是如此。

cues.en: He reminds you of the old Chinese logographs and sound meaning combinations.
cues.zh: 他让你想起古汉字以及音义结合的方式。

cues.en: Those are still useful to his court, to a point. You see, Chinese has these nice word units one after another.
cues.zh: 对他的朝廷来说，这些东西仍有用，但只在一定程度上。你看，中文有这样一个接一个整齐的词单位。

cues.en: But Korean, he boasts, has these elegantly complex words with different pieces and endings.
cues.zh: 但他夸耀说，韩语有这些优雅复杂的词，由不同的部件和词尾构成。

cues.en: Fitting Chinese writing to Korean grammar hasn't been easy.
cues.zh: 把中文书写套用到韩语语法上并不容易。

cues.en: He tells you of a people across the sea who've gone through a similar struggle.
cues.zh: 他跟你讲起海对岸一个民族，也经历过类似的挣扎。

cues.en: The Japanese simplified Chinese characters by turning them into a fixed syllabary,
cues.zh: 日本人简化汉字，把它们变成一套固定的音节文字，

cues.en: which they now use alongside the Chinese characters.
cues.zh: 如今他们把这套音节文字和汉字一起使用。

cues.en: So they have these syllable characters and these thousands of Han characters.
cues.zh: 所以它们既有这些音节字符，又有成千上万个汉字。

cues.en: They use the Han characters for the meaning heavy components, the vocabulary terms. Then they use the syllabary to write little grammatical words and word pieces or new vocabulary
cues.zh: 他们用汉字来承载语义较重的部分，也就是词汇术语；然后用音节文字来写小的语法词、构词成分或新词汇，

cues.en: words that don't historically have their own Chinese logograph.
cues.zh: 也就是历史上没有对应汉字的新词。

cues.en: Such a complicated system, gentlemen.
cues.zh: 先生们，这系统可真复杂。

cues.en: The king has an almost puzzled look, like he's holding back a punch line.
cues.zh: 国王一脸近乎困惑的表情，像是在憋着一个包袱。

cues.en: He recounts how in old Japan, women wrote entire books using only the syllable characters because writing with the traditional Han characters was seen as the masculine thing to do. But he knows of another land.
cues.zh: 他讲述在古日本，女性只用音节文字就能写出整本书，因为用传统汉字书写被视为男性该做的事。但他知道另一个国度。

cues.en: He's heard exotic tales of the West where people write out all of their sounds logically.
cues.zh: 他听说过西方的一些奇闻异谈，那里的人把所有发音都按逻辑写出来。

cues.en: He pauses.
cues.zh: 他停顿了一下。

cues.en: He can't quite grasp this himself.
cues.zh: 他自己也不太能理解这一点。

cues.en: You snicker as you think back on how you saw the alphabet develop with your own eyes in your journeys.
cues.zh: 你暗自窃笑，回想起旅途中亲眼看着字母表一步步发展起来的情景。

cues.en: You would know.
cues.zh: 你会知道的。

cues.en: So you sit down and show him how to write every vowel and consonant with the alphabet. A couple dozen shapes and you can write any sound. You smile and think, so simple.
cues.zh: 于是你坐下来，教他用字母表写出每个元音和辅音。几十个字形，就能写出任何声音。你微笑着想，真简单。

cues.en: But he lets out an unimpressed
cues.zh: 但他发出一声不以为然的

cues.en: sigh.
cues.zh: 叹息。

cues.en: Why do all the characters look so different, so haphazard?
cues.zh: 为什么这些字母看起来都这么不一样，这么杂乱无章？

cues.en: I mean, you make f and v by putting your bottom lip against your top teeth. The only difference is that your throat vibrates when you say v.
cues.zh: 我是说，发 f 和 v 时都要把下唇抵住上齿。唯一区别是，发 v 时喉咙会振动。

cues.en: He quizzes you. Why do you write f and v? And he goes on interrogating you. What about b? Why does it look that way when it's just taking the v sound and saying it through smacked lips?
cues.zh: 他考你：为什么把 f 和 v 写成这样？接着又追问：那 b 呢？它明明只是把 v 的音用双唇一闭发出来，为什么形状却是那样？

cues.en: Seems you underestimated the king. He doesn't want any old alphabet.
cues.zh: 看来你低估了这位国王。他想要的可不是随便一套字母表。

cues.en: He wants a writing system that shows the various features of sounds, that the sound is made in your throat against your teeth, made with your lips, and so on. He puts his brightest scholars to work, giving them the humble name of the hall of worthies.
cues.zh: 他想要一套能体现声音各种特征的书写系统：音是在喉咙里、抵着牙齿、用嘴唇发出的，等等。他让最聪明的学者们投入工作，还给他们起了个低调的名字——集贤殿。

cues.en: In go the experts and out comes another major
cues.zh: 专家们一介入，就出现了另一个重大的

cues.en: moments in the history of writing.
cues.zh: 书写史上的时刻。

cues.en: They develop Korean Hangul,
cues.zh: 他们创造了韩文 Hangul，

cues.en: a featural alphabet.
cues.zh: 一种特征字母表。

cues.en: Every syllable gets separated out into its own block. The syllables consonants and vowels will be written side by side within that block. Each consonant and vowel letter inside that block will be shaped according to its features.
cues.zh: 每个音节都会被划分到自己的方块中。音节中的辅音和元音会在该方块内并排书写。方块内的每个辅音和元音字母都按其特征来决定形状。

cues.en: So here are the consonants that get pronounced with the lips. See the similar lip shape?
cues.zh: 所以，这些就是用嘴唇发音的辅音。看到相似的唇形了吗？

cues.en: Here's g and here's k.
cues.zh: 这是 g，这是 k。

cues.en: Again, similar sounds, similar shape.
cues.zh: 还是相似的声音，相似的形状。

cues.en: The featural alphabet was so simple and straightforward that one of the king's historians almost dared people to learn it. If you're smart,
cues.zh: 这种特征字母系统简单直接，国王的一位史官甚至向人们叫板，让他们来学它。你要是聪明，

cues.en: you can learn it in one morning. If you're a fool, it'll take you ten days.
cues.zh: 一个上午就能学会；要是笨，就得花上十天。

cues.en: Not everyone's jumping on the Hangul easy train.
cues.zh: 可不是所有人都愿意搭上韩文这班“易学”快车。

cues.en: Community accessible writing bothers traditionalists
cues.zh: 大众都能学会的文字让传统派很不安，

cues.en: who skip out on the innovation and keep using Chinese characters fitted to Korean, Hanja, or Han characters even into the nineteen hundreds.
cues.zh: 他们不参与这项创新，继续使用为韩语改造的汉字（Hanja），甚至到20世纪还在用汉字。

cues.en: Still, for the rest, writing is easier than ever. It has its first rock star. It even gets its own holiday.
cues.zh: 不过，在其他方面，写作比以往任何时候都更容易。它有了第一位摇滚明星。甚至还有了自己的节日。

cues.en: Oh, writing. You've come a long, long way from pictographs in a cave.
cues.zh: 哦，文字。从洞穴里的象形符号一路走来，你真是走了漫漫长路。

cues.en: The day that Thoth invented writing, Thamus warned him that he discovered a drug that would make people lose touch with themselves.
cues.zh: Thoth 发明文字那天，Thamus 警告他：他发现的是一种会让人迷失自我的药。

cues.en: If you're still watching, you took Thoth's pill and saw for yourself the effects it really had.
cues.zh: 如果你还在看，说明你吞下了 Thoth 的药丸，并亲眼看到了它真正的效果。

cues.en: It started with visual depictions of the world, pictographs,
cues.zh: 最初是世界的视觉描绘，即图画文字，

cues.en: signs for ideas and thoughts, ideographs,
cues.zh: 用来表示思想和想法的符号，即表意文字，

cues.en: then a transformation from picture writing to true writing with symbols that stand for words, logographs.
cues.zh: 然后从图画文字转变为真正的文字，用代表词语的符号，即表词文字。

cues.en: Using those word symbols to stand for similar sounding words,
cues.zh: 用这些词符来表示读音相似的词，

cues.en: rebus,
cues.zh: 即画谜，

cues.en: then those sound alikes became syllable characters,
cues.zh: 随后这些同音词变成了音节字符，

cues.en: syllabaries,
cues.zh: 即音节文字，

cues.en: consonant characters, abjads,
cues.zh: 辅音字符，即辅音音素文字，

cues.en: and then consonant and vowel characters,
cues.zh: 然后是辅音和元音字符，

cues.en: alphabets,
cues.zh: 即字母文字，

cues.en: or even consonant and vowel syllables,
cues.zh: 甚至辅音和元音音节，

cues.en: alpha syllabaries.
cues.zh: 即元音附标文字。

cues.en: And if things get really linguistic, savvy alphabets become all featureal, characters grouped by their phonetic properties.
cues.zh: 如果真从语言学角度看，精明的字母表会变得完全以特征为基础，字符按语音属性分组。

cues.en: Along the way, writing had to deal with tensions and take sides.
cues.zh: 一路走来，文字必须处理各种张力并选边站。

cues.en: Should it represent meanings or sounds?
cues.zh: 它该表意还是表音？

cues.en: Should it benefit the reader or the writer?
cues.zh: 它该利于读者还是写者？

cues.en: Contain maximum information about every sound, or just enough to recognize the shape of a word? Should it be flexible and creative, or rigid and consistent?
cues.zh: 是包含每个声音的最大信息量，还是只够认出一个词的形状？它该灵活而有创造性，还是固定而一致？

cues.en: How do physical techniques shape it? Oh, and who did it first?
cues.zh: 物理技术如何塑造它？哦，还有，谁最先做出来的？

cues.en: Who did it best?
cues.zh: 谁做得最好？

cues.en: Maybe you've learned to make some sense out of the chaotic noise of world writing systems.
cues.zh: 也许你已经学会从世界文字系统混乱的噪声中理出一些头绪。

cues.en: Maybe you can appreciate some of the problems each one solves, the traditions it captures,
cues.zh: 也许你能体会到每种文字系统解决了哪些问题、承载了哪些传统，

cues.en: the ambiguities it creates.
cues.zh: 又制造了哪些歧义。

cues.en: Or perhaps it's more comfortable just to close your eyes and wake up back at home, looking at your familiar characters of your familiar writing system plastered across your favorite websites.
cues.zh: 又或者，更舒服的做法是闭上眼睛，醒来时已回到家中，看着熟悉的文字系统里那些熟悉的字符，铺满你最喜欢的网站。

cues.en: Still, somehow you can't even look at that the same way. It's just one invention among many in the long history of this language technology we call writing.
cues.zh: 可不知为何，你就是没法再用同样的眼光看待它。它不过是我们称之为书写的语言技术漫长历史中的众多发明之一。
